newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary grains futures down sharply.
newsitem.headline: Hungary grains futures down sharply.

text.p: Hungarian grains futures fell on Thursday following Wednesday's price falls on world markets and on good crop prospects, traders said.
Milling wheat and feed wheat futures dropped by the daily limit of 400 forints for almost all maturities.
"Chicago (wheat futures prices on Wednesday) fell like stone," said Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle Tozsdeugynoki Rt. "Crop outlooks are very good and the weather is perfect, too."

He added that Hungarian wheat futures prices were at about world market levels, but were still considered relatively high as the country was likely to be able to export wheat but transport costs would increase the prices.
Milling wheat futures closed at 22,500 forints for the July maturity, down 400 forints, and finished at 23,840 for December, down 380, while the May 1998 maturity remained unchanged at 25,700.
Maize and feed barley futures, which usually move together, also dropped sharply for almost all maturities on expectations of a large crop, dealers said.
Grains futures turnover on the BCE, which received momentum from world market price movements, soared to 647.9 million forints, or 1,366 lots, from 318.4 million forints, or 616 lots, on Wednesday.
